import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Difference of digit sums in base 3 and base 2

Difference of sums of digits of $n$ in ternary and in binary:
$$a(n) = \sum \mathrm{digits}_3(n) - \sum \mathrm{digits}_2(n).$$

*References:*
- [A180017](https://oeis.org/A180017)-/

namespace OeisA180017

/-- Difference of sums of digits of $n$ in ternary and in binary. -/
def a (n : ℕ) : ℤ :=
  (Nat.digits 3 n).sum - (Nat.digits 2 n).sum

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_0 : a 0 = 0 := by norm_num [a]

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_1 : a 1 = 0 := by norm_num [a]

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_2 : a 2 = 1 := by norm_num [a]

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_3 : a 3 = -1 := by norm_num [a]

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_4 : a 4 = 1 := by norm_num [a]

/--
"This sequence is positive on average, since 1/log(3) > 1/log(4). Do all integers appear
infinitely often?" - Charles R Greathouse IV, Feb 07 2013-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem conjecture (z : ℤ) : Set.Infinite {n : ℕ | a n = z} := by
  sorry

end OeisA180017

review.notes: All seven declarations match the source. Lean confirms that both digit sums are cast to ℤ before subtraction, so negative values are preserved. The five tests were independently reproved, and all 10,001 values in the OEIS b-file matched. A scratch proof also verifies that the infinite-fibre condition means occurrences at arbitrarily large indices. The empty digit list at n = 0 correctly has sum zero. OEIS HTML access was blocked, so the complete entry was read through its official data mirror. The paper linked from A037301 explicitly proves the z = 0 case; no resolution of the full every-integer question was found in the consulted sources. Scratch checks compile successfully, and the reviewed file matches its committed hash.
